answer: Each new agent must redeem a one-time postal pearl: a paper token mailed only to a government-listed residential address. A rotating grove of notaries hashes the address, occupant name, and a 30-day cooling nonce, then admits only the first redemption per postal hash in a calendar year. The applicant locks 400 POA for six epochs. If a second token is later redeemed from the same address hash, or if two keys share a device-plus-egress harbor cluster after admission, both bonds are slashed and the postal hash is frozen for a year. Shared mailrooms and virtual mailboxes are rejected at issuance.
